stem.en: The Damodarpur copper plates of Kumāragupta I record a district office of five members: the head district officer, the chief banker, the chief caravan trader, the chief artisan and the chief of revenue collection. What does this list show?

text.en: Only officers sent from the capital could take part in district government.
The king himself sat in each district office and decided its cases.
Districts had no officers of their own and were run by traders.
Leading residents such as the banker, the trader and the artisan worked alongside the district officers.

explanation.en: The list has a head district officer and a chief of revenue collection, and also a banker, a caravan trader and an artisan. This fits the account that district officers often decided after consulting important residents such as bankers, caravan leaders, artisans and scribes.

hints.en: Count how many of the five were trading or craft people.
The district still had a head officer, so option c cannot be right.
